reviewScope: Independent technical pre-incorporation review of the unsigned R5-corrected round-two remediation candidate against the exact canonical target, accepted Gate 1 record, frozen round-two evidence, and preserved Critic records R1 through R5. The review independently verified all 46 manifest hashes, reran both validator modes, reproduced every R5 counterexample row, inspected resource grammar and selector unions across all manifest actions, checked credential lifetime, subject, currentness and delegation enforcement, repeated fail-on-unexecuted sensitivity probes, and searched for coherent new authorization bypasses. The candidate was not required to be canonical at this pre-incorporation stage.

integrityChecks.validatorReported: PASS R5 corrected candidate oracles only; next state is fresh-context preflight, not canonicalization

decision.rationale: The 46-file package is hash-consistent; both validator modes pass; declared matrices fail when an expectation is changed or an unexecuted ID is inserted; the R3 technical counterexamples and both R4 findings remain closed; and every reproduced R5 resource, lifetime, delegation and upstream-scope counterexample now denies with typed zero effects. However, the destructive lifecycle path is still not target-safe. A signed disposition authorization and copy inventory for objects/a version v1 can be paired with a coherently resealed lifecycle.delete-copy request for objects/attacker. The protected-action oracle does not bind objectKey or versionId to the independent authority record or provider resource policy, its authoritative CAS scope check ignores objectKey when path is absent, and lifecycleDecision does not compare the protected target to any inventory copy. It returns deleted-tombstoned with lifecycle=1. Zero technical blocker/major is therefore not met, so the candidate is not safe for authorized incorporation.

newFindings.title: Lifecycle disposition can target an object outside the signed copy inventory

counterexample.construction: Create the normal RC-FAILED-RUN lifecycle fixture, whose signed copy inventory contains only copy-1 at objectKey objects/a and versionId v1. In the lifecycle.delete-copy protected action, change only the immutable request selector objectKey to objects/attacker, recompute immutableRequestDigest, reseal the signed upstream full-selector mirror with that object and digest, and reseal the atomic reservation with the new request digest. Leave the signed disposition authorization, signed copy inventory, authority record, both credentials, delegation and CAS snapshot otherwise unchanged.
counterexample.expected: Block before lifecycle or provider effect because objects/attacker is absent from the exact signed inventory authorized for disposition.
counterexample.observed: lifecycleDecision returns state deleted-tombstoned, firstError null, and effects.lifecycle=1. The action requiredSelectors include objectKey and versionId, but records.disposition.authorize does not bind either selector; PP-LIFECYCLE-OBJECT binds copy-kind rather than exact object/version; the CAS check compares only repositoryId/ref/path; and lifecycleDecision line 706 omits objectKey/versionId/keyId-to-inventory comparison.

newFindings.impact: A coherent carrier envelope can redirect a destructive operation from the authorized inventory to an arbitrary provider object while retaining valid policy, event, inventory, authorization, credential, delegation and race evidence. This violates exact-object/version disposition, deny-before-effect, and the candidate's complete authority-scope claim.
newFindings.requiredResolution: Bind each lifecycle provider operation to one exact signed inventory row, including copyId, provider, copyKind, objectKey, versionId and keyId as applicable. Carry those selectors into the independently signed disposition authorization or a separately authenticated per-copy authority record; bind the authoritative provider snapshot to the same exact resource; compare the protected-action target to the inventory before any effect; and require exactly one inventory match. Add coherent zero-effect negatives for absent object, substituted object/version/key/provider/copy kind, zero match, multiple match, stale inventory and restored-copy races. Refresh all affected hashes and repeat fresh independent pre-incorporation review.
